title: Grades 3–5 Mini Test — Speaking: A Day at School
tier: Classroom practice; not an ACCESS tier
overview: A short speaking practice with four tasks: describe, tell a story, explain, and give your opinion. Look at the pictures, plan, and speak in full sentences.

sections.title: A Day at School
sections.directions: Look at each picture. Read how the model student started. Plan your ideas, then say your answer out loud in full sentences. Use the word bank to help you.

items.title: The Lunchroom
passage: A model student, Lucía, started like this: "I see four students at a long table."
Now it is your turn. Plan your ideas, then say your answer aloud in full sentences.
items.adminScript: Look at the picture of the lunchroom. What do you see? What are the people doing? Take a moment to plan. Then say your answer aloud in full sentences.
items.prompt: Look at the picture of the lunchroom. What do you see? What are the people doing?
items.responseLabel: Planning notes (then say your answer aloud)
sayFor: name at least three people or things
use place words like behind and next to

models.B: I see students eating lunch at a table. A girl has milk and a boy has an apple. A worker serves food.
models.C: In the lunchroom, four students are sitting at a long table with their lunch trays. One girl is holding up her milk, and the boy next to her is holding an apple. Two friends are talking to each other. Behind the counter, a lunch worker is serving food, and there is a trash can and a recycling bin by the wall.

items.correct: Strong answer (model): In the lunchroom, four students are sitting at a long table with their lunch trays. One girl is holding up her milk, and the boy next to her is holding an apple. Two friends are talking to each other. Behind the counter, a lunch worker is serving food, and there is a trash can and a recycling bin by the wall.
items.hint: Look at the table first, then the counter, then the wall.
items.support: Use the word bank and the sentence frames. Say your answer out loud. Listen to the models to hear how answers grow.

picture.alt: A school lunchroom. Four students sit at a long table with lunch trays. One girl holds up a carton of milk, a boy holds up an apple, and two friends talk to each other. A lunch worker serves food behind a counter. A gray trash can and a blue recycling bin stand by the wall.

items.title: My Morning
passage: A model student, Tariq, started like this: "First, the boy wakes up when the alarm clock rings."
Now it is your turn. Plan your ideas, then say your answer aloud in full sentences.
items.adminScript: Look at the four pictures. Tell what the boy does in the morning. Use first, next, then, and finally. Take a moment to plan. Then say your answer aloud in full sentences.
items.prompt: Look at the four pictures. Tell what the boy does in the morning. Use first, next, then, and finally.
items.responseLabel: Planning notes (then say your answer aloud)

models.B: First, the boy wakes up. Next, he brushes his teeth. Then he eats breakfast with his sister. Finally, he waits for the bus.
models.C: First, the boy wakes up and stretches when his alarm clock rings. Next, he brushes his teeth at the bathroom sink. Then he eats a bowl of cereal at the table with his little sister. Finally, he puts on his backpack and waves when the yellow school bus comes to the bus stop.

items.correct: Strong answer (model): First, the boy wakes up and stretches when his alarm clock rings. Next, he brushes his teeth at the bathroom sink. Then he eats a bowl of cereal at the table with his little sister. Finally, he puts on his backpack and waves when the yellow school bus comes to the bus stop.
items.hint: Say one sentence for each picture. Start with an order word.
items.support: Use the word bank and the sentence frames. Say your answer out loud. Listen to the models to hear how answers grow.

picture.alt: Four pictures in order. 1: A boy wakes up in bed and stretches when his alarm clock rings. 2: He brushes his teeth at the bathroom sink. 3: He eats a bowl of cereal at the table with his little sister. 4: He waits at the bus stop with his backpack and waves as the yellow school bus comes.

items.title: After Lunch
passage: A model student, Hana, started like this: "After lunch, students should put their bottles in the recycling bin."
Now it is your turn. Plan your ideas, then say your answer aloud in full sentences.
items.adminScript: Look at the picture of the lunchroom again. Explain what students should do with their things after lunch. Tell where each thing goes and why. Take a moment to plan. Then say your answer aloud in full sentences.
items.prompt: Look at the picture of the lunchroom again. Explain what students should do with their things after lunch. Tell where each thing goes and why.
items.responseLabel: Planning notes (then say your answer aloud)
sayFor: tell which bin each thing goes in

models.A: Trash in trash can. Milk in blue.
models.B: After lunch, students should put trash in the trash can. Then they put the milk carton in the recycling bin. This keeps the lunchroom clean.
models.C: After lunch, students should clean up their own spot. First, they put the empty milk carton in the blue recycling bin, because it can be made into something new. Then they throw food wrappers in the gray trash can. Finally, they bring their tray back to the counter. This is important because it keeps the lunchroom clean for the next class.

items.correct: Strong answer (model): After lunch, students should clean up their own spot. First, they put the empty milk carton in the blue recycling bin, because it can be made into something new. Then they throw food wrappers in the gray trash can. Finally, they bring their tray back to the counter. This is important because it keeps the lunchroom clean for the next class.
items.hint: Use order words to explain each step.
items.support: Use the word bank and the sentence frames. Say your answer out loud. Listen to the models to hear how answers grow.

picture.alt: A school lunchroom. Four students sit at a long table with lunch trays. One girl holds up a carton of milk, a boy holds up an apple, and two friends talk to each other. A lunch worker serves food behind a counter. A gray trash can and a blue recycling bin stand by the wall.

items.title: Reading Alone or Together?
passage: A model student, Ngozi, started like this: "I think reading with a buddy is better."
Now it is your turn. Plan your ideas, then say your answer aloud in full sentences.
items.adminScript: Look at the picture of the reading corner. Is it better to read by yourself or with a buddy? Tell why. Take a moment to plan. Then say your answer aloud in full sentences.
items.prompt: Look at the picture of the reading corner. Is it better to read by yourself or with a buddy? Tell why.
items.responseLabel: Planning notes (then say your answer aloud)
items.responsePlaceholder: I think it is better to read ___.
frames: I think it is better to read ___.

models.B: I think it is better to read with a buddy because we can help each other. Also, we can talk about the book.
models.C: I think it is better to read by myself. One reason is that it is quiet, so I can focus on the story, like the girl on the beanbag. Another reason is that I can read at my own speed. Reading with a buddy can be fun, but I understand more when I read alone.

items.correct: Strong answer (model): I think it is better to read by myself. One reason is that it is quiet, so I can focus on the story, like the girl on the beanbag. Another reason is that I can read at my own speed. Reading with a buddy can be fun, but I understand more when I read alone.
items.hint: Choose one. Then use "because" to give two reasons.
items.support: Use the word bank and the sentence frames. Say your answer out loud. Listen to the models to hear how answers grow.

picture.alt: A classroom reading corner with a bookshelf. On the left, a girl reads a book by herself on an orange beanbag chair. On the right, two boys sit together on a blue rug and read one book together.
